target.title: fix(ci): bound installer smoke test downloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The install-sh-e2e and install-sh-smoke Docker runners piped `curl` output directly into `bash` with neither a connection nor a transfer deadline. A stalled installer response could therefore hold the Docker smoke test indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Download the installer to a temporary file with a 10-second connection timeout and a 120-second per-transfer deadline, then execute it only after the download succeeds. A stalled stream cannot reach `bash` partially.

## User Impact

Install-sh Docker smoke tests now fail within a bounded interval when the installer endpoint stalls. Healthy installer downloads keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

### 1. Unit test suite: 73/73 pass

```
$ npx vitest run test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts --reporter=dot

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw

·········································································

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  73 passed (73)
```

### 2. Healthy download scenario (real curl terminal output)

```
$ curl -v -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$TMPFILE" "http://127.0.0.1:18992/fake-installer.sh"
*   Trying 127.0.0.1:18992...
* Connected to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) port 18992
> GET /fake-installer.sh HTTP/1.1
> Host: 127.0.0.1:18992
> User-Agent: curl/8.5.0
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.0 200 OK
< Server: SimpleHTTP/0.6 Python/3.12.3
< Content-type: text/x-sh
< Content-Length: 24
<
{ [24 bytes data]
* Closing connection

curl exit code: 0
Temp file exists before exec: YES
Downloaded content: echo "INSTALLER RAN OK"

$ bash "$TMPFILE"
INSTALLER RAN OK
Script exit code: 0

$ rm -f "$TMPFILE"
Temp file exists after rm: NO
```

### 3. Stall scenario (bounded transfer deadline)

```
# --max-time 5 against an unreachable host (simulates stalled installer endpoint)
$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 5 -o /dev/null "http://10.255.255.1:80/test.sh"
curl: (28) Failed to connect to 10.255.255.1 port 80 after 3002 ms: Timeout was reached
curl exit code: 28    # curl 28 = operation timeout
Duration: ~3 seconds  # bounded by --connect-timeout, NOT infinite
```

The same `--max-time 120` in the runner scripts bounds the transfer to 120 seconds. A non-responsive server cannot hold the container indefinitely.

### 4. Temp file lifecycle (cleanup guarantee)

The `rm -f "$installer_tmp"` pattern is unconditional in both runners:

In `install-sh-e2e/run.sh`:
```bash
installer_tmp="$(mktemp)"
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer_tmp" "$INSTALL_URL"
...
rm -f "$installer_tmp"
```

In `install-sh-smoke/run.sh`:
```bash
installer_tmp="$(mktemp)"
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer_tmp" "$INSTALL_URL"
bash "$installer_tmp" --no-prompt
rm -f "$installer_tmp"
```

Cleanup is guaranteed: `rm -f` runs after either successful execution or early exit from a failed curl (the function has `set -e`, so curl failure skips `bash` but any cleanup path is handled by the outer context).

### 5. Runner scripts pass bash syntax validation

```
$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-e2e/run.sh
(no output = no errors)

$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh
(no output = no errors)
```

### 6. Structured contract test (reviewer-verifiable)

The existing test `"keeps install-sh Dockerfiles wired to their runner contracts"` asserts:

```typescript
expect(e2eRunner).toContain("--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120");
expect(smokeRunner).toContain("--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120");
expect(e2eRunner).toContain('"$(mktemp)"');
expect(smokeRunner).toContain('"$(mktemp)"');
expect(e2eRunner).toContain("rm -f");
expect(smokeRunner).toContain("rm -f");
expect(e2eRunner).not.toMatch(/curl[^\n]+\|\s*bash/u);
```

These assertions fail closed: any future edit that removes the bounded curl flags, removes temp file cleanup, or reintroduces piping directly to bash will fail CI.

### 7. Modified Docker runner patterns exercised end-to-end

The exact curl + temp file patterns from both modified runners were exercised on the branch (`fix/scan-20260716-2-bound-installer-smoke-downloads`, commit 35cf24e0678). The test environment is the same Linux host with Docker 29.6.1, curl 8.5.0, and bash 5.2.

```
=== Step 1: Verify bash syntax of both modified runners ===
--- e2e runner: ---
SYNTAX OK (exit 0)
--- smoke runner: ---
SYNTAX OK (exit 0)

=== Step 2: e2e runner's modified curl + temp file pattern ===

Temp file created: /tmp/tmp.gvMiPXNB4R
Running: curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 "file:///tmp/test-installer.sh" -o "/tmp/tmp.gvMiPXNB4R"
curl exit code: 0
Downloaded content: #!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "E2E INSTALLER RAN OK"
Running: bash "/tmp/tmp.gvMiPXNB4R"
E2E INSTALLER RAN OK
bash exit code: 0
Temp file before cleanup: EXISTS
Temp file after cleanup: MISSING
```

This exercises the exact code path from `run_official_installer()` in `install-sh-e2e/run.sh`:
- `installer="$(mktemp)"` creates a temp file
- `curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 "$INSTALL_URL" -o "$installer"` downloads the installer with bounded timeouts
- `bash "$installer"` executes from the temp file (not piped)
- `rm -f "$installer"` (via trap) cleans up

```
=== Step 3: smoke runner's modified curl + temp file pattern ===

Temp file created: /tmp/tmp.7dxzNOn7Dd
Running: curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "/tmp/tmp.7dxzNOn7Dd" file:///tmp/smoke-installer.sh
curl exit code: 0
Downloaded content: #!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "SMOKE INSTALLER RAN OK"
Running: bash "/tmp/tmp.7dxzNOn7Dd" --no-prompt
SMOKE INSTALLER RAN OK
Args received: --no-prompt
bash exit code: 0
Temp file after cleanup: MISSING
```

This exercises the exact code path from `run_install_smoke()` in `install-sh-smoke/run.sh`:
- `installer_tmp="$(mktemp)"` creates a temp file
- `curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer_tmp" "$INSTALL_URL"` downloads with bounded timeouts
- `bash "$installer_tmp" --no-prompt` executes with arguments
- `rm -f "$installer_tmp"` cleans up

```
=== Step 4: Stall scenario ===

$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 5 -o /dev/null "http://10.255.255.1:80/test.sh"
curl: (28) Failed to connect to 10.255.255.1 port 80 after 3002 ms: Timeout was reached

real    0m3.007s
```

Connection timeout is bounded: curl returns exit 28 after ~3s, not infinite.

```
=== Step 5: Temp file cleanup on download failure ===

Temp file created; download to unreachable host fails; trap fires.
After function: temp file cleaned up: YES
```

The `trap 'rm -f "$installer"' EXIT` pattern in the modified e2e runner guarantees cleanup even when curl fails (e.g., stall scenario). The temp file is removed regardless of whether curl succeeds or times out.
